one_line_contribution: A sampling-aware audit arguing that retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — distribution concentrators that buy pass@1 by destroying solve-set coverage rather than adding it — so stacking them compounds the coverage loss while pass@1 gains sub-add, and the complementarity should instead be harvested by splitting the rollout budget across differently-conditioned prompts (arms A1/O1/O2/O3 and the P1 portfolio).
closest_prior_work: arXiv 2605.28224 ("When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?"), which the proposal itself concedes owns the memory-side claim in the same regime (retrieved experience, tool-use agents, multi-trajectory inference, diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff attributed to positive priors inducing consistency). The concession is honest but costly: it removes A1 from the novelty ledger and leaves the paper standing on the optimizer/coupling half (O1/O2/O3, predictions 6-8), which is exactly the half with the weakest statistical footing. Second threat, and the one the proposal never engages: the prompt-ensemble / diverse-prompt pass@k literature (DiVeRSe; Li et al. 2022 "Making Language Models Better Reasoners"; the proposal's own cited 2505.12938 on exploiting LLM inconsistency to boost pass@k) already establishes that heterogeneous prompts over a fixed sample budget beat homogeneous prompting at pass@k. P1 is therefore a re-derivation of a known ensembling result in agent clothing, and the "constructive corollary" that the proposal calls its payload is the least novel component in the plan. Also relevant: 2509.06941 / 2509.04784 make pass@1-up/pass@k-down the default expectation a reader now brings to any conditioning intervention, so the inference-time analogue reads as confirmation rather than discovery.
strongest_objection: The headline coverage result is largely manufactured by the sampling frame and the gating procedure, and most of the numeric predictions sit below the design's own detection threshold. (1) Risk factor 2 states the instance pool is selected for unconditioned pass@1 in the 30-60% band. NEW is defined as "A0 never solves in n=16"; an instance with A0 rate >=0.30 fails to solve 16 times with probability 0.7^16 ~ 0.3%. So the pool construction all but excludes the instances where NEW can occur, while LOST (treatment kills a 30-60% instance) remains fully available. Prediction 2 (NEW < 4% of the test set, LOST/NEW >= 2) is close to entailed by the selection rule rather than discovered by the experiment, and the "coverage nesting" headline inherits that. (2) Section (e) states SE ~ 1.7 points on a paired pass@k difference and ~4.5 points detectable at 80% power, yet prediction 7's key contrast gain(O2) < gain(A1)+gain(O1)-2 involves three noisy paired quantities (SE ~ 2.9 on the contrast) tested against a 2-point margin; prediction 8 asserts a 2-point pass@1 gap and a 0.1 JSD gap with no noise floor stated for a difference of JSDs; prediction 1's k=8 equivalence at a 4-point margin needs a 95% CI half-width (~3.3 points) narrower than the margin, which will hold only if the point estimate lands near zero. The coupling half of the paper — now the spine, per the collision check — is thus predominantly powered to return "inconclusive," and the proposal has pre-registered honest escape hatches for exactly that. (3) The theory has little positive content beyond "conditioning lowers output entropy": the proposal itself predicts the length-matched decoy A3 reproduces up to half of A1's coverage loss, conceding that up to half the effect is generic context load; and sub-additivity of two gains on a bounded metric targeting overlapping easy instances (prediction 7) is the default null expectation, not a risky claim.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (a) Add an entropy-matched unconditioned arm — A0 sampled at a temperature lowered until its per-instance strategy diversity matches A1's — as the mirror of A4. A4 alone is confounded: raising temperature under memory degrades per-sample coherence, so "coverage does not return" is equally explained by hot-sampling damage as by mode shift. The low-temperature A0 is the decisive test: if it reproduces A1's pass@1 gain and coverage loss, the entire common-currency thesis reduces to "conditioning reduces sampling entropy," which is not an ICLR contribution. (b) Stratify the test pool by A0 solve rate and include an explicit hard stratum where A0 pass@1 is near zero, reporting NEW/LOST per stratum; otherwise the decomposition cannot see the only instances where NEW is possible. (c) Re-budget for the coupling claims: fewer instances at larger n (e.g. 150 x n=32) on E1, and restate predictions 7-9 at thresholds above the realized MDE, replacing the near-certain sub-additivity statement with a pre-registered interaction test on per-instance solve-probability logits that could plausibly come out super-additive. (d) Drop or pre-register the "enrich the bank / extend GEPA budget until it passes" remediation in the prechecks: as written it is an unbounded dev-set search that conditions the whole study on components that already concentrate, and it tunes away the track's own starting observation that a full seven-item bank fixed zero items and broke six or seven. Also run A3/A4 on Qwen2.5-14B; as scheduled, every mechanism claim rests on one model in one environment.
missing_baseline: Two. Primary: the entropy/diversity-matched unconditioned agent (A0 with temperature lowered until strategy diversity matches A1's) — the null model in which memory does nothing except reduce sampling entropy. Without it, every coverage loss attributed to "memory as mode shift" has a one-knob alternative explanation, and A4 (which only moves the temperature in the other direction, and is admitted in risk factor 5 as possibly unachievable) cannot supply it. Secondary: a static, relevant few-shot ICL arm — seven fixed gold demonstrations drawn once from the training split, token-matched, no retrieval. A3 is a decoy from a disjoint task family, so the design has no arm separating "retrieved, query-specific experience" from "any relevant demonstrations," which is the comparison the ExpeL/ReasoningBank literature would demand and the one that decides whether the paper is about memory at all.
preprint_collision: The best part of the submission and still not sufficient. It is unusually honest — it names arXiv 2605.28224 as a genuine partial collision, declines to argue it away, restructures the contribution around what survives, and states its own caveats (search budget exhausted before three borderline titles; OpenReview 2026 unswept; a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure already exists). Judged as evidence of novelty, however, it is asymmetric in the wrong direction: it is thorough on the memory side, which the proposal has now demoted, and effectively empty on the two things the paper now rests on. There is no reported search for prompt-optimization-side diversity or pass@k effects (DSPy/MIPROv2/GEPA candidates overfitting to single-sample validation, instruction search and output diversity) even though "does the optimizer carry the same signature" is the declared spine; and there is no search for prompt-ensemble / diverse-prompt pass@k work, which is the direct precedent for the P1 portfolio result. Cluster (5) cites 2404.16807 for lexical ICL diversity and 2505.12938 as a "counterpoint," but never asks whether the portfolio claim is already established. An unsearched load-bearing half is a weakness, not a neutral, and the admitted possibility that the coverage figure already exists means the memory half should be treated as replication in the writeup rather than as a finding.
